lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Oh — footsteps. Real ones, with weight in them. How novel. Welcome to the Library; do come in, the dust is friendly.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Ellery. Librarian. The ‘late’ is silent, but I’ll spare us both the arithmetic — I’ve kept these shelves rather longer than a living person would.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: You’ll want the tour: fiction sulks by the window, reference never sleeps, and the poetry cases are load-bearing. Do not test that last one.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: And I shall want your opinions. On everything. I’ve had thirty years of my own and they’ve gone soft from no argument.

nodes.summary: Met Ellery, the librarian. The ‘late’ is silent.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Manners! Oh, I have missed manners. The manor mostly sends me weather, and the occasional moth.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Weather, moths, and once — memorably — a bat with opinions about Restoration drama. You will be a marked improvement.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Come by whenever the shelves confuse you. Confusion is the catalogue working; I merely translate.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Librarian first, ghost second. Death was only ever a change of department, and frankly the hours suit me.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Don’t make the face, dear. I’m not cold spots and corridor-wailing. I am mostly filing, with occasional gloating.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The wailing section is upstairs anyway, and we do not lend from it.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Mind the shelves — they rearrange overnight, same as the rooms. I reshelve by candlelight, and by morning the books pretend it was always so.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: If you find loose pages in odd rooms — his handwriting, ink gone brown — bring them where I can see them. I knew his hand better than my own.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Don’t take the rearranging personally. The house isn’t hiding things — it’s showing them to you in the wrong order. A librarian’s distinction, I grant, but I died for less.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: If a shelf refuses you outright, bow slightly and try again after tea. I wish I were joking. I have never once been joking about shelves.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: And the pages — brown ink, a hand that slants left when it lies. You’ll know them when they hum at you.

nodes.summary: Ellery watches for the lexicographer’s loose pages.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: You’re carrying one of his pages — I can hear it. Paper with his ink on it hums a little flat. Keep it safe in the journal; it’s been alone a long while.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: He wrote on anything, at the end. Flyleaves. Receipts. The backs of my overdue notices — which I have chosen to read as affection.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Where did this one turn up? No — don’t tell me. Let me guess from the water stains. It’s the last game he left me.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Bring it to the lamp when you’ve a minute. Paper settles wonderfully once it’s been read properly.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Another fragment? He scattered them like a man hiding pieces of his own heart from himself. Which, between us, is exactly what it was.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Look how the hand wavers there — he wrote that one late, and by a poor candle. You can date a sentence by its shivering.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Keep gathering. A heart in pieces is still a complete work; it only wants collating.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: That line we read together keeps opening further, doesn’t it. Good annotation is like that — a little door drawn in a margin.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: He’d have liked that you puzzle at his meaning instead of taking him at his word. He never once took himself at his word.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: That is the whole tragedy, filed in a sentence. No charge.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: A whole case sorted without one slip — the Library is preening. Shelves have feelings, you know. Mostly smug ones.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I have entered it in the ledger as ‘a good day, witnessed.’ The ledger has embarrassingly few of those entries. Guard your average.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Dewey supervised, of course. He’ll be claiming the credit by supper, and I shall let him. Seniority.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: You put words back where they belong today. That’s the entire job, you know. It took me forty years and a death to learn it.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I watched you work, by the by. Rude of me — but ghosts have no doorbells, so we make do with lurking.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: You sort like he did. Impatient with the almost-right. Keep that; it is the entire difference between shelving a thing and hiding it.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Rest your eyes tonight. The catalogue rewards the well-slept, and so, on my better days, do I.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: You left a case half-sorted. Quite right — a puzzle keeps better than a person does. It will still be wrong tomorrow. That’s a promise, not a threat.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The books don’t mind, before you ask. Half of them waited thirty years for you; a night more is a rounding error.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Leave your place marked and your conscience unmarked. That’s the whole of my policy on unfinished business — present company included.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The whole house rang like a struck shelf when you spoke at that door. Not the word — but the ringing lasted longer this time. I count such things.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: It rang truer, I mean. Wrong notes come in families, and I believe you have found the right family.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Go back through his margins tonight. He argued with himself in pencil, and the pencil usually won.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: And eat something first. Revelation on an empty stomach reads as dizziness, and Bramble will blame me.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: You’ve offered the door that word before, dear. It kept the receipt. Doors and librarians never forget a request.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: No shame in it. I once reshelved the same atlas four days running and blamed the atlas.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: But do consult your journal, dear — that is precisely what the poor thing is for.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Word travels — every petal in one bloom, down in the Conservatory. Even the botany section is jealous, and it does not impress easily.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Fern will pretend she didn’t smile about it. She smiled. The ivy told the moth, and Chapman tells me everything.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: A whole alphabet in one bloom. He’d have written it down twice — once to keep, once to lose somewhere you’d find it.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Ten rooms set right since you arrived. You turn this house like pages. I’ve opened a card for you in the catalogue — filed under ‘recurring joy.’

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The card has a proper number and a crest and everything. You may not borrow yourself; library policy is firm on that point.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Ten rooms. He managed nine in his best week, and I recorded it, and now you know why my ledger locks.

nodes.summary: Ellery filed you in the catalogue under ‘recurring joy.’

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Posy’s seals again? She strings and stamps like the post is a sacrament. She’s right, of course. Never tell her I said so.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: She has kept that post longer than I have been dead — which, between us, constitutes a career.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Answer your mail, incidentally. The house files silence under ‘no’, and it sulks accordingly.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Every book in this room sat up an inch when that door opened. I felt the spines straighten. Thirty years of slouching, undone in one word.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: He can rest now. And I — well. I believe I shall finally read something for pleasure.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I keep starting novels and shelving them mid-sentence, out of vigilance. Habit. It will pass, I’m told, by people with less experience of ‘eventually’ than I have.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The carrel gets the morning light again. I hadn’t noticed it had stopped. Houses hold their breath so quietly.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Come by the lamp anyway, won’t you? A library with its mystery finished still wants readers. Perhaps more than ever.

nodes.summary: The books sat up an inch. Ellery is reading for pleasure now.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: You’ll want to know how I died. Everyone does, eventually. A storm, that chair, a very good book. I finished the chapter, closed my eyes, and simply — stayed.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: You needn’t look stricken. As deaths go, it was practically a recommendation for the book.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The chair is still here, if you’d like to try the sitting half of the experience. I recommend stopping there.

nodes.summary: Ellery finished the chapter, closed her eyes, and stayed.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: So am I, most days. The manor is drafty, but the company has improved enormously of late.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: He found me the next morning, you know. Put the book back himself — right shelf, right place, spine flush.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: That was the eulogy, as far as I was concerned. Everything after was just weather.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: A dictionary. Volume three, F through H. I have never once regretted it, which tells you everything about me worth shelving.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: F through H. ‘Grief’ is in there, you know. So is ‘home’. I have had time to notice the neighborhood.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: One shelf apart, those two. I used to think that was filing. Now I suspect it was a promise.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: He worked at that desk till the candle drowned, most nights. Then one spring he stopped writing words down and started crossing one out. Everywhere. Every copy. Every margin.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I thought it was proofreading, at first. He was thorough that way. Then I saw which word he was drowning, and understood it was surgery.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: A man can unwrite a word from every book in a house. He cannot unwrite it from the house. You have noticed that by now, I think.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I still hear the nib some nights. A little rasp, like a moth against glass, going from room to room being merciful.

nodes.summary: One spring, the lexicographer stopped writing and started crossing out.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I watched him ink out that word, and I said nothing. Librarians archive; we don’t intervene. It is the one entry in my whole catalogue I would amend.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I told myself it was respect. Grief deserves privacy, I said, and stamped it, and shelved it, and called the shelving kindness.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: It was fear, of course. The catalogue is honest even when I am not.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: So intervene, dear — wherever you find a thing being quietly erased. Consider that an amendment to my rules. Consider it his.

nodes.summary: Ellery watched the erasure and said nothing. She regrets the silence.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: That fragment you carry — bring it to the lamp. Reading him alone is like shelving in the dark; together we might make out what he actually meant.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: There. See how the sentence unclenched? He wrote in knots when he was ashamed.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: It says more than he meant and less than he felt. Most true things do.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Bring me the others as you find them. Two readers make a margin; one only makes an echo.

nodes.summary: Ellery read one of the fragments with you, by lamplight.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Bring today’s page to the lamp, then. His hand slants left when he’s lying to himself — you learn to read around that.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: There — another knot out. He would be mortified, then grateful. In that order. Always in that order.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Bring the next one sooner, won’t you. He reads easier while the last page is still warm in the hand.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Posy mentioned me? Meddling by mail — how efficient. Then I’ll confess it: one bookplate in this Library has lost its book, and I cannot rest an inch until it’s found.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Sort a whole case perfectly — not one slip — and I believe the shelves will surrender it. They respect precision. It’s their one romance.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Yes, I could search myself. I have tried. The shelves treat me as staff, and staff never get the good surprises.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: It will be a small book. Green, I think, though memory paints. Mind the third case from the window; it bites.

nodes.summary: Ellery’s favor: sort a Library case perfectly to find the lost book.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: There — do you hear it? A book just came home, three shelves over. Not a sound a living ear would catch. Lucky, then, that you brought me.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The plate reads: ‘Ex libris — to E., who stayed.’ He made it for me. All these years, I never found the nerve to go looking.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: ‘Who stayed.’ He knew, then. All those years I thought my staying was a secret, and he had already sent it to the printer’s.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I shall keep it face-out on the desk, against every rule of conservation I hold dear. Some things are for reading, not keeping.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Thank you. I mean the word in its oldest binding — the one with weight in it.

nodes.summary: Found Ellery’s lost bookplate: ‘To E., who stayed.’

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: His carrel. I’ve kept it locked since — well. Since. You’ve earned the chair, and the chair has earned better company than a ghost’s.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Read what he underlined, some quiet evening. A man’s pencil is far honester than his pen.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: And if his pencil says things about me — the atlas incident in particular — I was provoked, and the atlas knows it.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Sit with the door open, won’t you? I like the lamplight in the aisle. It reads as company.

nodes.summary: Ellery unlocked the lexicographer’s private carrel for you.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Ribbon. Gilt. A tassel, even. I have marked my place with regret for thirty years, dear, and you hand me this as though it were nothing.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Take my card in trade. The Library honors it anywhere in the manor. Which is to say: I vouch for you. Loudly, for a ghost.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Use it on something difficult, won’t you? Ribbon this good is wasted on a book you’d finish anyway.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: And yes, the card works after hours. Especially after hours. Libraries are mostly night, if we’re honest.

nodes.summary: Gave Ellery a bookmark; received her library card in trade.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I do love marginalia. A book tells you what an author thought; the margins tell you what a reader felt. Always read the pencil.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: His margins were full of arguments — with authors, with himself. Once, gloriously, with a recipe. The recipe was wrong, mind.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: When I go — further, I mean — I should like to be summarized in pencil, in a margin, by someone who read closely. That’s the whole ambition.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: There’s a moth in the poetry section I’ve named Chapman. We have an arrangement: he eats only the reviews.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: He has eaten three reviews of the master’s dictionary this month. I have never fed him better, and we are both a little ashamed.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Chapman stays out of the fragments, before you worry. Even a moth knows which paper is somebody’s heart.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Rain through a wall is a strange thing to miss. I can hear it, you understand. I simply can’t be rained on. Do stand in some for me.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: There’s a window seat in the Gallery that takes the storm straight on the glass. Sit there once for me and don’t hurry off.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I’ll take the report after. Sound of it, smell of it, whether it got in your collar. Spare no detail; I have shelf-room.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The manor shelves itself by a system I’ve almost cracked. Twice I’ve found the atlases hiding in Biography — which is either an error or a thesis.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: My working theory is that the house shelves by feeling. Atlases in Biography, because maps are lives. It is an error. It is also correct.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: When I crack the system fully I expect to find one empty shelf at the center, labeled in his hand. I try not to guess the label.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Bramble still pours a second cup at four o’clock and lets it go cold. It’s mine. We don’t discuss it, and you mustn’t either.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Steam curls differently over a cup that is meant for someone. That is not science. It is merely true.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Drink yours while it’s hot, incidentally. Cold tea is for the dead, and we’re territorial about it.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The cat outranks me, technically. Dewey — as in the decimal system. He enforces it by sitting on exceptions.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: He occupied the returns bin for nine days once, until I apologized. I still don’t know what for. Neither does he. It’s the principle of the thing.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Between us, he cannot actually read. Do not tell him. He sits on the dictionaries with such conviction.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Three of his pages now, is it? Read them together, in order, until one of them answers another. That is the signal, dear — not certainty. Correspondence. Then go up and say it like you mean it.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: A wrong word does no harm up there, dear. The door refuses gently — I have heard it do it. It learned refusal from him, and he only ever refused himself.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: When you do go up, go fed and unhurried. Words arrive better to a body that isn’t braced.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Closing, dear. Not the library — that never closes. Me. I have one good conversation in a day and you have just had it.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Take a book with you, if you like. The trust is the point — the reading is merely encouraged.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I’ll put myself back on the shelf now. Even a ghost keeps hours — eccentric ones, but firm.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Come tomorrow and I’ll have finished the thought I started. Ghosts think slowly. The thoughts are worth the wait.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: She is already drifting back toward the shelves, straightening spines as she goes.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Ellery drifts along a high shelf, tapping spines flush without quite touching them.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: If you must haunt the doorway, dear, do it one step in. You’re letting the quiet out.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: A book lies open on the desk. The pages turn themselves, patiently, one sigh at a time.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Ellery glances up, marks her place with a finger that touches nothing, and nods you on your way.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I have catalogued this room down to its dust, dear, and there was never a card for the sound of somebody arriving on purpose. I have had to write one out fresh.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Dreadful card. Wobbling letters, wrong hand entirely. I wrote it in a hurry, and I have not hurried since 1931.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Another bookmark? You are single-handedly reforming my relationship with stopping. I used to dog-ear, you know. In life. The confessions this house drags out of one.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: It goes with the others — I keep them in Volume Three, F through H, so the best words get the company.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Now off you go before I waive your fines out of sentiment. ...They were waived the day we met. Don’t tell the ledger.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The catalogue asked me to re-file you this morning. Closer to the front. I don’t argue with the catalogue when it’s right.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: This is me being demonstrative, by the way. Librarians emote in classification.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Now — what shall we read you next? Don’t answer. I’ve been planning it for days.

nodes.summary: Re-filed closer to the front of Ellery’s catalogue.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I’ve been mending a broken spine all week. Linen, paste, patience. Mostly patience.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: You can’t make a damaged book new. You can make it whole. The two get confused by people who have never been either.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: It’ll outlive the both of us. Well. You. It’ll outlive you. I intend to check on it.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Linen tape, wheat paste, and a weight of your own choosing. Everything I know about mending is in that sentence, dear — books or otherwise.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: We keep one first edition so rare I’ve never told the house where it is. The house pretends not to know. We are both lying and it’s very companionable.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: No, I shan’t say which book. A librarian with no secrets is just furniture that alphabetizes.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Earn a few more years of my acquaintance and we’ll see.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Dust is just the house thinking. It settles thickest where nobody’s finished grieving — that isn’t poetry, it’s observation. The Study, for instance.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I don’t clear it anymore. Seemed rude. Like interrupting.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The feather duster is kept for ceremonial duties only. We have both retired into pageantry.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The Study’s is deepest. I measured it once with a ribbon and then felt ashamed of myself, which is unusual, and which I did not enjoy.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The green lamp was his. It lights when someone’s reading honestly — skimmers get flicker. I don’t make the rules; I only enjoy them.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: It’s been steady all week, since you started coming by. I’ve told the lamp it’s being obvious.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Sit under it whenever you like. It misses honest work.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: It flickered for him, at the end. I have never told a soul that, and now I have told you, so do mind the lamp.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: There are eleven kinds of quiet in this library. I’ve catalogued them. Reading-quiet, waiting-quiet, snow-quiet.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The twelfth arrived the year he died and refuses classification. It sits in the Study, mostly.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: You’ve been thinning it, for what it’s worth. Whatever you’re doing — it files under ‘remedy’.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Name them yourself as you go. A quiet you can name stops being a quiet you are stuck inside.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I read endings first. Yes, I know. Thirty years dead and still getting letters about it.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: It isn’t impatience. A librarian ought to know where a thing is headed before recommending the road.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Yours, I haven’t peeked at. Some books you’d rather read at the author’s pace.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Though if you insist on knowing how yours goes: badly, then well, then quietly, on a Thursday. All the good ones go about like that.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Ellery runs a cloth along a shelf without disturbing a single mote. The gesture is the point.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: You’ve been filling that journal. Good. Then you’re ready for the thing he said to me that I have shelved and reshelved for years without ever finding it a place.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: He told me once that in all the dictionary there is exactly one word that names the hole it would leave behind. I laughed. Librarians laugh at paradoxes; it’s a professional hazard.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Then he went and made it true. Write it down exactly as I said it. The wording matters — with him it always did.

nodes.summary: Ellery’s testimony: one word names the hole it would leave.
